purpose: Record intentional M2A flow-semantics revisions after the behavior-preserving M1 migration.

entries.question: What happens to a direct nullable-variable narrowing after that variable is assigned?
entries.decision: A successful assignment or numeric compound assignment to a direct variable invalidates every active non-null narrowing for that resolved binding. The binding returns to its declared or inferred type until a later supported nil check establishes a new narrowing. The invalidation remains effective in enclosing active flow regions that may observe the mutation, while facts introduced only in a nested region are discarded when that region ends.
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, active branch narrowing survived an assignment to the same binding.
entries.rationale: The assignment mutates the shared binding cell, so a prior proof about its value is no longer valid. Clearing the fact is conservative and preserves the existing rule that only direct simple-variable nil checks establish narrowing.
affected_consumers: nullable type-error and positive recheck fixtures
entries.compatibility_consequences: Programs that use a nullable binding as non-null after assigning it must re-check the binding. No parser, IR, bytecode, VM, field/index, loop, post-branch, alias, or call behavior changes in this slice.
entries.migration: Keep the existing branch-fact producer and add scoped invalidation records beside it. TypeChecker records the invalidation only after normal assignment validation succeeds; no duplicate semantic or lowering path is introduced.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1662 cases, the focused FlowFacts CTest passes, the named positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: There is no compatibility implementation to delete in this slice. The old behavior is replaced only after the shared invalidation record and positive/negative mutation fixtures pass.

entries.question: Can a function or closure body inherit nullable narrowing from its definition-site control flow?
entries.decision: No. Every function body is checked with an empty active flow-fact environment. Function parameters and facts established inside the body are still checked normally, while a captured binding is observed through its declared or inferred type until the body establishes its own supported narrowing.
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, checkFunctionBody inherited active facts from an enclosing if branch when a nested function was declared there.
entries.rationale: A function may execute after its definition-site branch has ended, and closures observe shared mutable cells. A definition-site proof cannot be treated as a proof at every later call site.
affected_consumers: TypeChecker function, method, and lambda body analysis
nullable closure-boundary type-error and runtime fixtures
entries.compatibility_consequences: Function bodies that relied on an outer nullable proof must add a local nil check or accept the nullable type. This slice does not infer call-site effects or invalidate caller facts when a closure may mutate a captured binding.
entries.migration: Wrap the shared checkFunctionBody entry point in a flow-fact isolation scope so named functions, methods, and anonymous functions use the same rule. Restore the caller state on success and exceptions.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1665 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named function-boundary positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The inherited-fact behavior is removed only after the shared function-body isolation and both compatibility fixtures pass.

entries.question: How does a resolved direct call affect nullable narrowing for captured local bindings?
entries.decision: When a resolved direct call targets a local function whose capture metadata names an enclosing binding, every active narrowing for each currently visible captured binding is invalidated after successful argument and call-shape checking. The rule is conservative because capture metadata records reads and writes together. Native, unresolved, indirect, callback, global-alias, and struct-method effects are outside this slice.
entries.owner: DeclarationIndex capture metadata, TypeChecker, and FlowFacts
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, a direct call to a closure that could assign a captured nullable binding left the caller's prior non-null proof active.
entries.rationale: A closure call can update a shared captured cell. Retaining a caller-side proof after that call is unsound; invalidating only captured local bindings avoids changing ordinary calls that cannot observe those cells.
entries.compatibility_consequences: Code that uses a captured nullable binding after a direct closure call must perform a fresh supported nil check. Calls to ordinary non-capturing functions retain existing narrowing behavior. Indirect/callback and global mutation effects remain deferred.
entries.migration: Reuse the already-collected direct call target and capture records; map captured declaration IDs back to visible TypeChecker bindings and invalidate their active facts after the call succeeds.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1668 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named captured-call positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old retained-proof behavior is replaced only after direct captured-call invalidation and its positive/negative fixtures pass.

entries.question: How does an indirect or dynamic function call affect active nullable narrowing?
entries.decision: After successful argument and call-shape checking, a call that is not resolved to a direct FunctionStmt target invalidates every active nullable narrowing. This includes aliases, anonymous function values, and unresolved or dynamic callees. Resolved direct FunctionStmt calls retain the precise captured-binding rule from M2A-FLOW-003; native stdlib fast paths and struct-method calls are outside this slice.
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, an indirect function call retained all caller-side nullable proofs, even when the function value could be a closure that mutates shared state.
entries.rationale: The current semantic model does not retain a complete function-value-to-capture effect summary for aliases or dynamic callees. Clearing every active fact is sound for this boundary and makes the uncertainty explicit without weakening precise direct-call handling.
affected_consumers: TypeChecker indirect and dynamic call checking
entries.compatibility_consequences: Code that uses a nullable binding as non-null after an indirect or dynamic call must perform a fresh supported nil check. Direct non-capturing calls retain unrelated facts, while native callbacks and struct-method effects remain deferred.
entries.migration: Use the existing direct-call metadata to distinguish resolved FunctionStmt targets from aliases and dynamic values. Invoke the shared all-fact invalidation primitive only after normal call validation succeeds; do not add a second call or lowering path.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1671 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named indirect-call positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old retained-proof behavior is replaced only after indirect-call all-fact invalidation and its positive/negative fixtures pass; a future effect-summary slice may replace the conservative rule.

entries.question: How does a callback-capable native collection helper affect active nullable narrowing?
entries.decision: After successful callback checking, an unshadowed native map, filter, flatMap, any, all, count, find, findIndex, or reduce call, including its built-in member-call sugar, invalidates every active nullable narrowing. Native calls without callbacks, namespace calls, enum variant constructors, and struct methods are outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker native callback paths and FlowFacts
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, native helpers that invoke callbacks retained caller-side nullable proofs even when a callback could mutate a shared captured cell.
entries.rationale: Callbacks may execute zero or more times and can be closures with shared mutable captures. The current model has no callback effect summary, so all-fact invalidation is sound and consistent across function-style and member-call native entry points.
entries.compatibility_consequences: Code that uses a nullable binding as non-null after a callback-capable native call must perform a fresh supported nil check. Non-callback native calls retain their existing flow behavior; struct-method effects remain deferred.
entries.migration: Classify callback-capable native names in the shared TypeChecker call paths, invalidate all active facts only after the helper and callback have passed normal validation, and exclude namespace/variant/struct metadata paths.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1674 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named native-callback positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old retained-proof behavior is replaced only after callback-capable native all-fact invalidation and its positive/negative fixtures pass; a future callback-effect summary may replace the conservative rule.

entries.question: How does a resolved struct-method call affect active nullable narrowing?
entries.decision: After successful argument and call-shape checking, every resolved struct-method call invalidates all active nullable narrowing. The rule is intentionally conservative because a method may mutate receiver fields or top-level state, while field/index narrowing itself remains unsupported. Unresolved member calls and future dynamic dispatch are outside this slice.
entries.owner: DeclarationIndex struct-method targets, TypeChecker, and FlowFacts
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, a resolved struct-method call retained caller-side nullable proofs even though method bodies could mutate shared receiver or top-level state.
entries.rationale: Struct methods have an implicit receiver and can perform field mutations that are not represented by the simple-variable capture metadata. Top-level bindings are also not method captures. Invalidating all facts avoids retaining proofs across either effect boundary without pretending to implement field/index narrowing.
entries.compatibility_consequences: Code that uses a nullable binding as non-null after a resolved struct-method call must perform a fresh supported nil check. Struct-method calls with no apparent mutation are conservatively covered by the same rule.
entries.migration: Reuse the existing StructMethod call target metadata and invoke the shared all-fact invalidation primitive only after normal method argument checking succeeds. Keep receiver field/index analysis unchanged.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1677 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named struct-method positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old retained-proof behavior is replaced only after resolved struct-method all-fact invalidation and its positive/negative fixtures pass; a future effect-summary and field/index slice may replace the conservative rule.

entries.question: When may a nil-check narrowing survive an if statement into its continuation?
entries.decision: For an if statement without an else whose then statement is guaranteed not to fall through through a return, returning block, or returning exhaustive match, the condition's else narrowings become active after the if. Facts are restored from before the terminating branch before the continuation is installed, so mutations on the dead path do not affect the live path. Explicit-else branches, loops, fields, and indexes remain outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker statement fall-through analysis and FlowFacts branch state
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, a returning nil guard did not preserve the false-branch non-null proof, so the continuation still saw the nullable declared type.
entries.rationale: A branch that cannot fall through removes its path from the continuation. Retaining the false-branch fact is sound, while restoring the pre-branch state prevents assignments or calls on the returning path from contaminating the live path.
affected_consumers: FlowFacts active narrowing snapshots and continuation append
entries.compatibility_consequences: After `if (value == nil) { return; }`, the continuation may use `value` as non-null. Equivalent guards with an explicit else, loops, fields, indexes, or non-terminating branches retain the existing conservative behavior.
entries.migration: Add a shared statement fall-through predicate and isolate the terminating branch with the existing scoped facts. Restore the pre-branch active facts and append only the condition's else facts after the branch succeeds.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1680 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named post-branch positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old missing-continuation-proof behavior is replaced only after terminating-guard state restoration and its positive/negative fixtures pass; explicit-else and loop joins require later slices.

entries.question: When may an explicit-else nil-check narrowing survive into its continuation?
entries.decision: For an if statement with an explicit else whose exactly one arm is guaranteed not to fall through through a return, returning block, or returning exhaustive match, the other arm's final nullable flow facts become active after the if. Both arms are checked from the same pre-branch snapshot plus their condition facts in isolated states. If both arms may fall through, the existing conservative behavior remains unchanged; loops, fields, indexes, and broader branch joins are outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker explicit-else arm isolation and FlowFacts continuation state
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, an explicit-else statement discarded the live arm's non-null proof even when the other arm returned, so the continuation still saw the nullable declared type.
entries.rationale: Only the non-terminating arm reaches the continuation. Checking both arms from the same isolated snapshot prevents a mutation or call on the terminating arm from contaminating the live arm, while installing the live arm's complete final state preserves its invalidations and facts.
affected_consumers: FlowFacts active narrowing snapshots, clearing, and continuation append
entries.compatibility_consequences: After `if (value == nil) { return 0; } else { ... }`, the continuation may use `value` as non-null. Explicit-else statements whose both arms fall through retain the existing conservative behavior, and a mutation or effect in the live arm prevents stale proofs from being retained.
entries.migration: Reuse the shared statement fall-through predicate. Check both explicit arms inside isolated FlowFacts states seeded with the pre-branch facts and condition facts, then clear and install only the final state of the arm that can reach the continuation.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1683 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named explicit-else positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old discarded-live-arm behavior is replaced only after isolated arm checking and its positive/negative fixtures pass; both-fall-through joins and loop joins require later slices.

entries.question: When may a while-loop condition narrowing be used in the loop body and after the loop?
entries.decision: For a while statement, the condition's true-branch nullable flow facts are active while checking the loop body and are discarded at the loop boundary. Body assignments and calls use the existing invalidation rules while those facts are active. C-style for, for-in, loop exits, and broader loop joins remain outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker while-body flow scope and FlowFacts branch facts
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, a nullable value guarded by a while condition remained nullable inside the loop body, even though the body is reached only after the condition's true result.
entries.rationale: The true branch is the only path entering each while iteration, so its direct-variable narrowing is sound for body checking. A loop may execute zero times or exit through break after a mutation, so the condition fact is not promoted beyond the loop boundary.
affected_consumers: FlowFacts scoped branch facts and mutation invalidation
entries.compatibility_consequences: A nullable binding may be used as non-null inside `while (value != nil) { ... }`, but remains nullable after the loop unless an independent fact is active. C-style for and for-in loops retain their existing behavior.
entries.migration: Reuse the existing if-condition branch-fact resolver and scope only its then facts around while-body checking with `FlowFacts::withNarrowings`; do not install those facts after the loop.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1686 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named while-body positive and post-loop negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old nullable body rejection is replaced only after scoped while-body facts and its positive/negative fixtures pass; other loop forms and loop joins require later slices.

entries.question: When may a C-style for condition narrowing be used in its loop body and after the loop?
entries.decision: For a C-style for statement with a condition, the condition's true-branch nullable flow facts are active while checking the loop body and are discarded at the loop boundary. Existing initializer and increment checking remains unchanged, and for-in, loop exits, and broader loop joins remain outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker C-style for condition/body flow scope and FlowFacts branch facts
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, a nullable value guarded by a C-style for condition remained nullable inside the loop body, even though the body is reached only after the condition's true result.
entries.rationale: The condition's true branch is the only path entering each C-style for iteration. Scoping that fact to the body preserves the proof without claiming that a loop exit or a later increment establishes a post-loop non-null state.
entries.compatibility_consequences: A nullable binding may be used as non-null inside `for ; value != nil; increment { ... }`, but remains nullable after the loop unless an independent fact is active. Initializer/increment effects and for-in loops retain their existing behavior.
entries.migration: Reuse the existing if/while condition branch-fact resolver and scope only the condition's then facts around C-style for-body checking with `FlowFacts::withNarrowings`; do not install those facts after the loop.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1689 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named C-style for-body positive and post-loop negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old nullable body rejection is replaced only after scoped C-style for-body facts and its positive/negative fixtures pass; for-in and loop-join rules require later slices.

entries.question: Which nullable facts survive an explicit-else statement when both arms may fall through?
entries.decision: When both explicit arms may fall through, only final nullable flow facts with the same resolved binding and mutually compatible narrowed types in both isolated arm states become active after the if. Facts present in one arm only or invalidated in either arm are discarded. Returning-arm joins continue to install only the live arm's final state; loops, fields, and indexes remain outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker explicit-else branch isolation/intersection and FlowFacts continuation state
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, an explicit-else statement discarded all branch-local final facts, even when both arms independently established the same nullable narrowing before falling through.
entries.rationale: A fact is sound after a branch only when every reachable arm preserves a compatible proof. Isolated checking prevents cross-arm mutation leakage, and intersecting final states avoids retaining a proof established on only one path.
affected_consumers: FlowFacts active-state replacement through clear and append
entries.compatibility_consequences: After both explicit arms independently narrow the same nullable binding, the continuation may use it as non-null. A one-sided proof, incompatible arm fact, or arm mutation leaves the binding conservative.
entries.migration: Reuse the isolated explicit-arm checking path from the returning-arm slice, intersect final states by resolved name and compatible type, then clear and install only the intersection for the continuation.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1692 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named explicit-else intersection positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old discarded-join behavior is replaced only after isolated branch intersection and its positive/negative fixtures pass; loop joins and field/index joins require later slices.

entries.question: When may a direct named-struct field nil check narrow the field value?
entries.decision: For a known named-struct field reached through a direct variable receiver, a nil comparison establishes a field-specific nullable narrowing in the active branch, loop body, or explicit-else continuation state. Field assignments conservatively invalidate all active nullable facts, root variable assignments invalidate related field facts, and nested fields, indexes, dynamic receivers, and alias-specific field precision remain outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker field target resolution, FlowFacts expression targets, and field mutation effects
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, `box.value != nil` did not narrow the known nullable field, so a non-null use of `box.value` remained a type error inside the guarded branch.
entries.rationale: A direct variable plus a statically known named-struct field provides a stable snapshot-local target key. Field writes may be observed through aliases, so the conservative all-fact invalidation rule avoids retaining any stale field or variable proof after mutation.
affected_consumers: FlowFacts expression-target branch facts and root-prefix invalidation
TypeChecker named-struct field reads and assignments
entries.compatibility_consequences: A known direct field may be used as non-null after a supported nil check. Field writes invalidate active facts, while nested fields, array indexes, dynamic receivers, and alias-specific precision retain the existing conservative behavior.
entries.migration: Keep variable resolver compatibility while adding an expression-target resolver for direct fields. Use the field fact for known field reads, invalidate all facts after field writes, and invalidate field-prefixed facts when their root variable is assigned.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1695 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named direct-field positive and mutation-negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old unsupported direct-field narrowing behavior is replaced only after target-key resolution, mutation invalidation, and its positive/negative fixtures pass; nested fields and index targets require later slices.

entries.question: When may a direct array element nil check narrow the indexed value?
entries.decision: For a known direct array variable and a compile-time non-negative integer literal index, a nil comparison establishes an index-specific nullable narrowing in the active branch, loop body, or explicit-else continuation state. Index assignments and compound assignments conservatively invalidate all active nullable facts, root array assignments invalidate related index facts, and dynamic indexes, map/range elements, nested targets, and alias-specific index precision remain outside this slice.
entries.owner: TypeChecker index target resolution, FlowFacts index facts, and aggregate mutation effects
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, `values[0]` did not narrow the known nullable array element, so a non-null use of the indexed value remained a type error inside the guarded branch.
entries.rationale: A direct array binding plus a normalized integer literal provides a stable snapshot-local target key. Index writes may be observed through aliases and dynamic access, so all-fact invalidation avoids retaining stale element or unrelated variable proofs after mutation.
affected_consumers: FlowFacts expression-target branch facts and root-prefix invalidation
TypeChecker direct array index reads and assignment effects
entries.compatibility_consequences: A known direct array element may be used as non-null after a supported nil check. Index writes invalidate active facts, while dynamic indexes, map/range elements, nested targets, and alias-specific precision retain the existing conservative behavior.
entries.migration: Reuse the expression-target resolver introduced for direct fields and add normalized integer index keys. Apply an active index fact to direct array reads, invalidate all facts after index writes, and invalidate index-prefixed facts when their root array binding is assigned.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1699 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the direct-index positive and mutation/dynamic negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old unsupported direct-index narrowing behavior is replaced only after target-key resolution, mutation invalidation, and its positive/negative fixtures pass; dynamic indexes and other aggregate targets require later slices.

entries.question: When may a supported while condition's false-branch fact survive a loop exit?
entries.decision: For a while loop whose condition produces an else narrowing, the else fact survives a normal condition-failure exit only when the body contains no break targeting the current loop. Continue, returns, and breaks belonging to nested loops do not block the rule. C-style for, for-in, and loop exits with a current-loop break remain conservative.
entries.owner: TypeChecker while-loop exit state and current-loop break detection
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, while-loop checking discarded all condition facts at the loop boundary, so a nullable value proven non-null by a condition-failure exit remained nullable after a no-break loop.
entries.rationale: A normal while exit is reached only after the condition evaluates false. Rejecting bodies with a current-loop break avoids treating an early exit as if the condition had been rechecked, while nested-loop breaks and continue statements preserve the outer loop's condition-failure boundary.
entries.compatibility_consequences: After a no-break `while (value == nil)` loop, the continuation may use `value` as non-null. A current-loop break, unsupported condition shape, C-style for, or for-in loop retains conservative nullable behavior.
entries.migration: Reuse existing FlowFacts condition analysis and scoped body facts. Detect break statements that target the current while loop, then append only the condition's else facts after a body check when no such break exists; nested loop and function boundaries stop the break scan.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1701 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the no-break while-exit positive fixture and current-loop-break negative fixture pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The old unconditional loop-boundary discard is replaced only after current-loop break detection, scoped body checking, and its positive/negative fixtures pass; C-style for, for-in, and broader loop joins require later slices.
